newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas rises again but volumes thin.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas rises again but volumes thin.

text.p: The IPE natural gas contract slowed right down on Friday after its record day on Thursday, as only 40 lots were traded.
But prices were higher in all traded periods, continuing the recent trend on both spot and futures markets.
December traded twice, reaching a new contract high of 15.70 pence a therm just before the close, while January also reached a new contract high of 18.75 pence, although only for five lots.
The other month to trade was October, which saw a single five lot trade at 11.15 pence a therm, up by 0.075 pence from Thursday's settlement.
Of the total 40 lots traded, 25 were done as a single trade in the morning, while the remaining 15 lots were in three separate deals all done in the last minute before the contract closed.

A spokeswoman for the IPE was not disappointed by the slow day following the record 960 lots done the previous day. "We are expecting it to be up and down," she said, adding that there are still not many companies trading the futures market on a daily basis.
